absent: Locking, concurrency and lifetime rules for programs, maps, links, tokens and iterators are absent from these fragments.
System-call dispatch, verification, privilege checks and full error codes beyond the noted flag and size rules are absent.
Helper argument lists, return values, allowed program types and runtime semantics are absent; only numeric identities are shown.
State machines for attach, detach, query, link update, test run and stream read are absent.
Exact byte sizes, cross-architecture padding and 32-bit compatibility rules beyond stated alignment and reserved bits are absent.
Meanings of attach types, query flags, token flags, stats types and descriptor-type enumerators are absent.

findings.text: The trailing portion of the union named bpf_attr groups one view per command plus a signed-load tail with fd_array_cnt, an aligned signature pointer, signature_size and signed keyring_id for verification. The whole object requires eight-byte alignment so all wide members stay naturally aligned.

The object view for pin and fetch holds pathname, bpf_fd, file_flags and signed path_fd. Resolution follows open-at directory semantics: path_fd is meaningful only with BPF_F_PATH_FD set in file_flags and must otherwise be zero, with AT_FDCWD assumed when the flag is absent.

The attach and detach view selects its target with target_fd versus target_ifindex, then holds attach_bpf_fd, attach_type, attach_flags, replace_bpf_fd, a relative choice of relative_fd versus relative_id and expected_revision for conditional replacement.

The test view named test holds prog_fd and retval, data_size_in with data_in and data_size_out with data_out, repeat and duration, ctx_size_in with ctx_in and ctx_size_out with ctx_out, plus flags cpu and batch_size. Output sizes act as both inputs and outputs and report short-buffer conditions.

The identifier view selects a start with start_id versus prog_id versus map_id versus btf_id versus link_id and returns next_id, with open_flags and fd_by_id_token_fd for token-gated lookup. The info view named info holds bpf_fd with info_len and an aligned info pointer.

The query view named query selects its target with target_fd versus target_ifindex, then holds attach_type query_flags and attach_flags, an aligned prog_ids pointer, a count choice of prog_cnt versus count, 32 reserved bits, aligned prog_attach_flags link_ids and link_attach_flags pointers and revision. The per-program flags array is output and is disallowed during an effective query.

The raw tracepoint view named raw_tracepoint holds name, prog_fd, 32 reserved bits and an aligned cookie. The BTF view holds aligned btf and btf_log_buf pointers with btf_size btf_log_size btf_log_level btf_log_true_size btf_flags and signed btf_token_fd, where the token descriptor is valid only with BPF_F_TOKEN_FD.

The task query view named task_fd_query takes pid fd and flags plus in-out buf_len and aligned buf whose meaning depends on probe kind as tracepoint name, kprobe symbol or uprobe filename. It returns prog_id, fd_type from the BPF_FD_TYPE family, probe_offset and probe_addr.

The link-create view named link_create combines a program-or-map choice of prog_fd versus map_fd, a target choice of target_fd versus target_ifindex, an attach_type and flags with a large option union. Options are target_btf_id alone, iter_info plus iter_info_len, a perf_event cookie named bpf_cookie, kprobe_multi flags cnt syms addrs and cookies, tracing target_btf_id plus cookie, netfilter pf hooknum priority and flags, tcx netkit and cgroup each with relative_fd or relative_id plus expected_revision, uprobe_multi path offsets ref_ctr_offsets cookies cnt flags pid and path_fd, and tracing_multi ids cookies and cnt. Cookies are opaque user values delivered to the program through get_attach_cookie.

Small views use fixed orders. Link update named link_update holds link_fd, a new choice of new_prog_fd versus new_map_fd, flags and an old choice of old_prog_fd versus old_map_fd used as expected value with replace. Link detach holds link_fd. Enable-stats holds type. Iterator create holds link_fd and flags. Program bind map holds prog_fd map_fd and flags. Token create holds flags and bpffs_fd. Stream read holds stream_buf stream_buf_len stream_id and prog_fd. Struct-ops association holds map_fd prog_fd and flags.

Cross-field rules govern the union. Path_fd must be zero unless BPF_F_PATH_FD is set. Btf_token_fd requires BPF_F_TOKEN_FD in btf_flags. Old descriptors in link update apply only when BPF_F_REPLACE is set in flags. Prog_attach_flags must not be supplied during an effective query. Data and context output lengths report required space on short buffers. Btf_log_true_size reports full material including terminator regardless of truncation or short fill.

Helper constants arise from a table pairing each base name with a fixed number plus callback macros that emit one BPF_FUNC prefixed enumerator per entry. An apply helper binds the table to the emitter and the collected enum named bpf_func_id ends with __BPF_FUNC_MAX_ID marking the range end.

The numbered helper table is declared effectively frozen, with new capability to be added as kfuncs carrying weaker stability instead of extending the numbers, alongside a pointer to Documentation/bpf/kfuncs.rst.

Checksum helpers use fixed values. BPF_F_RECOMPUTE_CSUM is bit zero and BPF_F_INVALIDATE_HASH is bit one. BPF_F_HDR_FIELD_MASK equals hexadecimal F. BPF_F_PSEUDO_HDR BPF_F_MARK_MANGLED_0 BPF_F_MARK_ENFORCE and BPF_F_IPV6 are bits four through seven. BPF_CSUM_LEVEL_QUERY BPF_CSUM_LEVEL_INC BPF_CSUM_LEVEL_DEC and BPF_CSUM_LEVEL_RESET are sequential values zero through three.

Tunnel helpers use fixed bits. BPF_F_TUNINFO_IPV6 is bit zero. BPF_F_ZERO_CSUM_TX BPF_F_DONT_FRAGMENT BPF_F_SEQ_NUMBER and BPF_F_NO_TUNNEL_KEY are bits one through four. BPF_F_TUNINFO_FLAGS is bit four in its own set.

Stack helpers combine a mask with option bits. BPF_F_SKIP_FIELD_MASK equals hexadecimal FF. BPF_F_USER_STACK is bit eight. BPF_F_FAST_STACK_CMP and BPF_F_REUSE_STACKID are bits nine and ten for the stack-identifier helper only. BPF_F_USER_BUILD_ID is bit eleven for the stack helper only. BPF_F_GET_BRANCH_RECORDS_SIZE is bit zero in its own set.

Perf and namespace selectors use fixed masks. BPF_F_INDEX_MASK covers all low 32 bits and BPF_F_CURRENT_CPU equals that mask. BPF_F_CTXLEN_MASK covers bits 32 through 51 for socket-buffer output. BPF_F_CURRENT_NETNS equals negative one.

Bits zero through twelve in order are BPF_F_ADJ_ROOM_FIXED_GSO, BPF_F_ADJ_ROOM_ENCAP_L3_IPV4, BPF_F_ADJ_ROOM_ENCAP_L3_IPV6, BPF_F_ADJ_ROOM_ENCAP_L4_GRE, BPF_F_ADJ_ROOM_ENCAP_L4_UDP, BPF_F_ADJ_ROOM_NO_CSUM_RESET, BPF_F_ADJ_ROOM_ENCAP_L2_ETH, BPF_F_ADJ_ROOM_DECAP_L3_IPV4, BPF_F_ADJ_ROOM_DECAP_L3_IPV6, BPF_F_ADJ_ROOM_DECAP_L4_GRE, BPF_F_ADJ_ROOM_DECAP_L4_UDP, BPF_F_ADJ_ROOM_DECAP_IPXIP4 and BPF_F_ADJ_ROOM_DECAP_IPXIP6. Length packing uses BPF_ADJ_ROOM_ENCAP_L2_MASK FF with shift BPF_ADJ_ROOM_ENCAP_L2_SHIFT 56 via BPF_F_ADJ_ROOM_ENCAP_L2 of length. BPF_ADJ_ROOM_NET and BPF_ADJ_ROOM_MAC are zero and one. BPF_HDR_START_MAC and BPF_HDR_START_NET are zero and one. BPF_LWT_ENCAP_SEG6, BPF_LWT_ENCAP_SEG6_INLINE and BPF_LWT_ENCAP_IP are zero through two.

BPF_F_SYSCTL_BASE_NAME is bit zero. BPF_LOCAL_STORAGE_GET_F_CREATE is bit zero with BPF_SK_STORAGE_GET_F_CREATE kept as an equal alias. BPF_RB_NO_WAKEUP and BPF_RB_FORCE_WAKEUP are bits zero and one. BPF_RB_AVAIL_DATA BPF_RB_RING_SIZE BPF_RB_CONS_POS BPF_RB_PROD_POS and BPF_RB_OVERWRITE_POS are zero through four. BPF_RINGBUF_BUSY_BIT is bit 31, BPF_RINGBUF_DISCARD_BIT is bit 30 and BPF_RINGBUF_HDR_SZ is eight.

BPF_SK_LOOKUP_F_REPLACE and BPF_SK_LOOKUP_F_NO_REUSEPORT are bits zero and one. BPF_F_BPRM_SECUREEXEC is bit zero. BPF_F_INGRESS and BPF_F_EGRESS for socket-buffer paths are bits zero and one while BPF_F_BROADCAST and BPF_F_EXCLUDE_INGRESS for express-data paths are bits three and four, with BPF_F_REDIRECT_FLAGS combining all four. BPF_SKB_CLOCK_REALTIME BPF_SKB_CLOCK_MONOTONIC and BPF_SKB_CLOCK_TAI are zero through two alongside deprecated BPF_SKB_TSTAMP_UNSPEC zero and BPF_SKB_TSTAMP_DELIVERY_MONO one.

The helper named __bpf_md_ptr defines an eight-byte aligned union holding either a typed pointer or a 64-bit placeholder for stable width. The record named __sk_buff starts with len pkt_type mark queue_mapping protocol vlan_present vlan_tci vlan_proto priority ingress_ifindex ifindex tc_index, a five-element cb, then hash tc_classid data data_end and napi_id.

The same record continues with family remote_ip4 local_ip4 remote_ip6 local_ip6 remote_port local_port data_meta flow_keys tstamp wire_len gso_segs sk gso_size tstamp_type and hwtstamp, with 24 reserved bits after the timestamp type. Address quads and remote values use network order while the local port uses host order, and the span from family through local_port is the portion described as visible to socket-socket program types.

The record named bpf_tunnel_key holds tunnel_id, a remote choice of remote_ipv4 versus remote_ipv6, tunnel_tos and tunnel_ttl bytes, a choice of tunnel_ext versus tunnel_flags where the latter is big-endian and the former exists for compatibility, then tunnel_label and a local choice of local_ipv4 versus local_ipv6.
The record named bpf_xfrm_state holds reqid, spi in network order, family, a reserved ext slot and a remote choice of remote_ipv4 versus remote_ipv6 kept in network order.

Layout rules preserve ABI stability. The outer union and metadata pointers require eight-byte alignment. Query and raw tracepoint reserve an unnamed 32-bit slot and the socket-buffer context reserves 24 bits after tstamp_type. Transform ext is padding for future use. BPF_SK_STORAGE_GET_F_CREATE remains an equal alias while new code must use BPF_LOCAL_STORAGE_GET_F_CREATE. Tunnel tunnel_ext remains for compatibility with tunnel_flags. Deprecated BPF_SKB_TSTAMP values keep old numbers.

Size edges need care. Undersized data_out and ctx_out report ENOSPC instead of silent truncation. Btf_log_true_size can exceed the supplied log size when truncated or fall short when underfilled. Prog_attach_flags are rejected during effective queries. Future BPF_SKB_CLOCK values unknown to a program must be deduced from direction and socket clock context.
